$comment: Canonical AiFinPay B2BSplitter registry — the single source of truth for the
addresses the SDK pays. The SDK's table is GENERATED from this file; never
hand-edit the generated copy, CI compares the two and fails on drift.
KEYED BY CHAIN AND ROUTE. From v1.3 a chain carries one splitter per protocol
route, because the fee split is immutable at construction and the two
protocols need different economics. A key is '<chain>:<route>' and selection
must use both. Never resolve a splitter by chain alone and never fall back
from one route to the other: the deployer used CREATE, so the same address
recurs on different chains for different routes — OP's merchant-aifp1 is the
same address as Base's agent-x402 — and an address alone therefore says
nothing about which economics apply.
'verified' records what was read FROM THE CHAIN on the stated date: the
deployed bytecode was fetched, the payment entrypoint selector was found in
it, and runtimeCodeHash is the keccak-256 of that exact bytecode. A missing
or stale runtimeCodeHash fails verification — an address alone says nothing
about what is deployed at it.
'owner' is read from the chain the same way, and is not decoration. The owner
can pause the contract, move the treasury and rewrite the stablecoin
whitelist, so every other pinned field is provisional until you know who
holds it. Every v1.3 route splitter must report the Safe in 'governance', and
that Safe's own signer set and threshold are then read on the same chain and
required to match exactly. A splitter not owned by that Safe can never have
settlementEnabled true, which is what keeps the EOA-owned legacy deployments
historical rather than payable.
'stablecoins' is the owner-mutable allowlist, pinned per chain from the
production deployment config and asked about token by token on chain. A
stable runtimeCodeHash proves nothing about it — setWhitelistedTokens does
not touch bytecode. null means the chain accepts no stablecoin: native only.
Nothing is trusted from one node. Every value is read from two independent
providers (distinct hosts) and must agree byte-for-byte; a disagreement is
a failure, not a vote. A chain with a single public provider declares
rpcQuorum 1 with a reason — it verifies, but can never be settlementEnabled
until a second independent endpoint exists.
'build' pins the reviewed source tree and toolchain. verify-build.mjs
recompiles and must reproduce every v1.3 runtimeCodeHash from it.
An unreachable RPC is NOT a pass. verify-registry.mjs exits non-zero when it
cannot reach a required chain, because 'we could not check' and 'it is fine'
must never produce the same result.
Version semantics: v1.1 exposes payMatic(address,address,string);
v1.2 payNative(bytes32,address,address,string);
v1.3 payNative((bytes32,address,uint256,address,uint256,string)) — tuple
argument, and GROSS-INCLUSIVE: the payer's amount already contains the fee.
Route semantics under v1.3:
merchant-aifp1 (100/0) — the agent pays the quoted gross amount, the
AiFinPay treasury receives 1%, the merchant receives 99%.
agent-x402 (0/0) — the provider receives 100% of the provider-defined
price and the AiFinPay fee is 0% for now. This route is NOT fee-on-top.
Fee-on-top, provider-preserving semantics arrive in a future contract
version when the AIFP-2 fee is activated; do not describe today's route
that way and do not convert this contract to it.
Entries marked superseded are retained deliberately. Historical deployments
are evidence and are never deleted; the v1.3 resolver never selects them.
NOTE the scope of settlementEnabled: it governs the v1.3 route resolver in
the SDK and nothing else. The legacy SDK path (SPLITTER_DEPLOYMENTS) and the
backend's SPLITTER_ADDRESS_* do not read this file and still settle live
traffic through the superseded polygon:legacy contract until cutover. A
'false' here is not a claim that a contract is switched off on chain — no
splitter can be switched off except by pause() — it is a claim that the NEW
path may not use it. AIFINP-213.
The Safe that owns every v1.3 route splitter. The owner controls pause and
unpause, the treasury address and the stablecoin whitelist, so an unverified
owner makes every other pinned field provisional: whoever holds it can change
them. verify-registry.mjs reads owner() from each live contract and requires
this address, then reads the Safe's own getOwners() and getThreshold() on that
same chain and requires this exact shape.
The signer set and threshold are compared exactly, never as a floor. A Safe at
the right address with the threshold lowered still reports the right owner
while meaning something entirely different, and 'threshold >= 2' is what let a
4-of-5 Safe silently pass as 3-of-5 in the production deploy script.
Threshold 3 of 5 is ADR-006.
A correct signer set is not, by itself, proof that only three signatures can
exercise the owner's powers. A Safe MODULE executes through the Safe without
any owner signature at all; a GUARD can veto or alter what executes; the
SINGLETON is the code the proxy actually runs; the FALLBACK HANDLER answers
calls the Safe itself does not. Each is therefore pinned and read live:
singleton from storage slot 0 and its code hash, the proxy's own code hash,
guard and fallback handler from their keccak-named slots, and
getModulesPaginated() which must return exactly the pinned list (empty).
reviewedNonce is the Safe nonce at the last review, per chain. The whitelist,
treasury and pause state can only change through an owner call, an owner call
can only come from the Safe, and every Safe execution increments nonce() —
so nonce unchanged since review proves none of them changed since review,
without scanning event history on nine chains. A higher nonce is not an
error in the Safe, it is a signal that governance acted: verification fails
until someone reviews what was executed and re-pins with --pin.
The reviewed source and toolchain that every v1.3 runtimeCodeHash must
reproduce from. A stable on-chain hash proves a deployment has not
changed; it does not prove the reviewed source produced it. verify-build.mjs
compiles contracts/ with exactly these settings, writes each route's
immutable profile into the compiled runtime at the positions the compiler
reports, hashes the result and requires it to equal the pinned hash.
contractsTreeHash is the git tree hash of contracts/ at review; any change
under contracts/ fails the gate until re-reviewed and re-pinned.

notSplitters.$comment: Recorded so nobody mistakes a Core deployment for a payment target. Neither exposes payMatic or payNative — paying these would not settle.

$policyFields: validFrom and validUntil are a POLICY review window, not chain state. They
cannot be read from a contract, so they are declared here and must be
renewed deliberately. An expired window fails validateQuotedNativePayment
with registry_entry_expired, which is intended: a route nobody has
re-reviewed should stop settling rather than drift on.
The window is 90 days from registry activation. Renewal and review are owned
by the Web3/CTO side under Governance Safe control.
settlementEnabled is deliberately false on every v1.3 entry at activation.
Deployed and verified is not the same as payable. A chain and route is
enabled individually, and only after a successful mainnet paid end-to-end
settlement on that exact route with verified balance deltas.
